function: above_phy, p. 3: the learned FedAvg-D3QN assigns resource blocks to ground D2D links (hypergraph coloring, fixed transmit power), a MAC scheduling decision, not control of an aerial link.
notes: Exclude, above_phy (first code that applies; there is a learned method, so no_learning does not). The learned FedAvg-D3QN chooses the resource block (RB) of each D2D link between ground IoT devices. p. 3: "N IoTDs are randomly distributed on the ground, and a self-organizing network is established using a D2D communication model"; p. 3: "each DL can occupy a maximum of one RB"; p. 8: "performs the corresponding RB selection operation". Transmit power is fixed, p. 6: "under the assumption that the transmission power of IoTD remains constant", and there are no beams, precoders, or antenna arrays, so the decision is MAC-layer channel assignment/scheduling posed as hypergraph node coloring (p. 5-6). The carve-out of above_phy for satellite and aerial links does not apply: the links that receive the learned allocation are terrestrial D2D links (p. 3: 3GPP TR 38.901 UMi path loss, "the connection between D2D pairs can be Line of Sight (LoS)"), while the UAVs, "stationed at predetermined locations", only collect training data and relay "the computed RB allocation results to the IoTDs" (p. 3); no learned power, beam, or resource control is applied to the IoTD-UAV, U2U, or NTN links (Fig. 1, p. 3). FedAvg averages the D3QN parameters digitally at a server (p. 10, eqs. 26-27), not over the air, so area 7 does not apply either. If the reviewer judged terrestrial RB allocation to be physical layer, the next code that applies would be function (not a problem of areas 1 to 7). The PDF matches the DOI: title and DOI 10.1109/JIOT.2024.3434713 on p. 1.
